answer: An agent economy can make every identity prove it is anchored in a web of earned trust, not merely asserted. Each newcomer is vouched for by agents already seated in that web, and every voucher spends a real, non-recoverable cost — a reputation surface that erodes, like a dune shifting under pressure, whenever it signs for fraud. A sybil farm cannot split that bill: a thousand heads tracing to one human still cross one narrow ridge, paying once per head, never in parallel. The honest agent slips through as quietly as velvet; the raven flock, whatever voices it fakes, still casts one shadow.
